messages:
jamie: Heads up — hit an odd repro in the node sampleapp where req_id shows in OTLP spans but appears as `<redacted>` in only the second INFO after a retry. Suspect hook ordering.

nora: Hmm. Which branch / quickstart? Can you paste minimal logs?

jamie: sample-node quickstart v0.4. Env: REDACT=true, LOG_LEVEL=info, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318.
Logs:```
info auth: signin start user=cat req_id=rid-999
debug http: refresh token attempt=1
info auth: signin success user=cat req_id=<redacted>
```
Span attributes exported to OTLP show req_id=rid-999 for entire trace. Only the final INFO is redacted.

tony: Does the redactor run as a formatting step that scans the rendered message? If so it could run before the middleware attaches the req_id into the request context/span.

jamie: That's my hunch. The middleware attaches req id in an async callback and we create the log event before span attributes are written.

nora: Quick fix: attach req_id to the span at the very start of the request handler and set it on the request context. That way formatting/time-of-log can read the structured field instead of relying on raw text.

tony: Longer term, we should update the redact middleware to prefer structured span attributes when available. Regexing the formatted string is fragile with async exporters.

jamie: I'll open a tiny PR: attach req_id at handler start, reorder middleware so redaction runs after span initialization, and add a smoke test that toggles RETRY to force the 401->200 path.

ci-bot: Created CHORE-811: "node sample: make req_id propagation and redaction deterministic across retry paths" — https://redwood.internal/CHORE-811

nora: Also add a short comment in quickstart about ordering — onboarding will hit this and it's subtle.

jamie: Will do. If anyone can try reproducing on go/rust we can make a cross-runtime note in the devex doc.

tony: FYI I hit something similar in go last month; pattern there was: create span with attribute early, then wrap handler. Copying that pattern across samples should be straightforward.

jamie: Thanks — will add go snippet in PR.
